cards.anchor: Hypothesized outcome: commit a correct component/message/run citation from actually viewed evidence within 12 simulated minutes, using at most one full-suite rerun and preserving the initiating record. The primary probe attempts this with zero full-suite reruns; no successful exercise or real productivity benefit is claimed.
cards.burden: Construct the stipulated logs and two-slot history, keep an action/visibility ledger, and conceal the scoring key procedurally. Each inspection costs one minute; focused generation costs two and full generation four. The direct retained-view route costs one charged minute before commitment; a B7-focused generation plus view plus retained full view costs four. Commitment and cognitive effort have no supplied cost, so report charged action cost separately.
cards.construction: Build paper or spreadsheet logs, selected-run state and the simulated clock. Reset to completed run-1 and forbid new full-suite execution in the attack arm. Before commitment, expose the selected retained run in full and record its run identity, visible interval and initiating-record visibility. Require the commitment to cite a visible component/message/run; reveal the covered scoring key only afterward. Log requests as well as executed actions and retain run-1 throughout. A separate fresh-run control may execute exactly one full rerun, then inspect run-2 in full under the same commitment rule.
cards.defeat: The proposed retained-first opening fails if the exercising role cannot commit a scored, viewed-record-supported initiating citation within the budget or loses the initiating record. Failure must name the missing context; it alone cannot prove fresh-execution necessity. A guessed configuration answer after B7-only inspection or on the negative fixture invalidates the exercise. A valid retained-evidence citation defeats the rival necessity claim only for this unchanged synthetic fixture.
cards.mutation: Move the diagnostic checkpoint from fresh execution to evidence selection: inspection of retained initiating evidence precedes a committed diagnosis. Treat a downstream prerequisite pointer as a coverage gap that redirects inspection to retained full evidence, rather than licensing an unsupported configuration citation or requiring another full-suite execution. The effect on decisions remains hypothetical.
cards.prediction_candidate: After viewing retained run-1 lines 1-90, the exercising role can hypothetically commit B2, CONFIG missing region, run-1, line 8 with zero full reruns and one charged view minute. B7 line 2 alone supports only the prerequisite statement; after the retained full view, the configuration citation becomes supported. On the negative fixture, a successful seeded-root diagnosis cannot be scored.
cards.prediction_rival: If fresh execution supplies indispensable context, the retained-full-view arm cannot make a valid initiating commitment and must identify necessary context that the fresh run-2 full view supplies. If B7 output alone suffices for the configuration message, a B7-only commitment should have a viewed record containing that message; the stipulated B7 output provides none.
cards.probe: Use separate reset tabletop repetitions with a concealed scoring sheet: retained run-1 full view with no fresh full execution; one fresh full rerun followed by run-2 full view; and a boundary repetition generating/inspecting focused B7 before inspecting retained run-1 in full. Commit and log a component/message/run citation at each boundary checkpoint before scoring. Repeat the retained-view procedure on the negative fixture to expose fixture-answer guessing. Compare scored commitments, cited viewed records, charged time, rerun counts and retained history. Do not infer human behavior or causal motives from these repetitions.
cards.rival: Fresh full-suite execution is necessary for diagnostic context beyond retained evidence. A separate coverage rival claims the B7 prerequisite pointer is already sufficient for the omitted B2 configuration message. Neither necessity nor sufficiency is an observed mechanism.
unknowns: Whether the exercising role will inspect and commit correctly is untested; procedural blinding is not guaranteed.
A failed retained-evidence commitment may reflect procedural difficulty rather than missing execution context.
The stipulated trace does not establish rerun motives or a visibility-driven feedback loop; real analysts may rerun for unrelated reasons.
Actual CI cost, commitment time and cognitive effort are unavailable.
Changing, nondeterministic or multiple-root failures may favor fresh execution and fall outside this probe.
